claim.why_it_matters: Both columns of the page are flattened to one indent level, so every sub-entry reads as a top-level entry.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of printed page 852 (PDF p874) shows a two-level index in both columns. Sub-entries are indented under their heads, for example 'INITIALIZE statement 457' under 'OBJECT-REFERENCE phrase', four entries under 'Obsolete language elements', 'Arithmetic/Boolean/Concatenation/Invocation/Logical/Relational' under 'Operators', and 'METHOD-ID paragraph 181' under 'OVERRIDE clause'. In page-874.md every line has the same 3-space indent and a trailing backslash, so the parent/child relation is lost. Read flat, 'INITIALIZE statement 457' or 'CALL statement 420' looks like a top-level entry, so the index meaning changes (which phrase the page refers to). No text is missing, and the index is non-normative, which makes this a structural defect and not a normative one. The quotes match both sources. A separate defect outside this claim: the markdown merges 'P PICTURE symbol 313' and 'p_cs_precedes 65' onto one line.
verdict.corrected_description: The two-level index hierarchy on this page (sub-entries indented under head entries in both columns) is flattened in the markdown: every entry carries the same indent, so sub-entries such as 'INITIALIZE statement 457' (under OBJECT-REFERENCE phrase) cannot be told apart from head entries. All of the text is present. Only the nesting is lost.
